{{Short description|Italian physicist and communist militant (1943–2025)}}
{{use dmy dates|date=October 2023}}
[[File:Franco Piperno 2.jpg|thumb|200px|Piperno in 2008]]  
'''Franco Piperno''' (5 January 1943 – 13 January 2025) was an Italian [[communist]] militant. He was an associate professor of [[Condensed Matter Physics]] in the [[University of Calabria]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.csdim.unical.it/scienzeformazione/programmi/piperno_f.pdf |title=Course held by Piperno |access-date=5 February 2011 |archive-date=22 July 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110722062126/http://www.csdim.unical.it/scienzeformazione/programmi/piperno_f.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Life and career==
Piperno was born in [[Catanzaro]] in a [[Italian Jewish|Jewish]] family. He graduated in physics at the [[University of Pisa]] and  was member of the [[Italian Communist Youth Federation|FGCI]] (Italy's communist youth organization). After his expulsion,<ref name="tramontopotop">{{cite news|last=Mazzocchi|first=Silvana|title=Da Valle Giulia al 7 aprile così tramontò Potere operaio|url=http://ricerca.repubblica.it/repubblica/archivio/repubblica/2007/01/18/da-valle-giulia-al-aprile-cosi-tramonto.html|accessdate=17 January 2011|newspaper=La Repubblica|date=18 January 2007}}</ref> in 1969 he was suspected of having sabotaged a [[Boston Chemical]] plant, which produced defoliant used in the [[Vietnam War]], but he was immediately released.<ref name="cattivimaestri">{{cite news|last=Mastrogiacomo|first=Daniele|title=Lui, il '68 e i 'cattivi maestri'|url=http://ricerca.repubblica.it/repubblica/archivio/repubblica/1996/05/07/lui-il-68-cattivi-maestri.html|accessdate=17 January 2011|newspaper=La Repubblica|date=7 May 1996}}</ref> In [[Rome]] he was an activist in the 1968 movement and in the summer 1969 he took part in the demonstration against [[Fiat]] in [[Turin]].

In the late 1969, with [[Oreste Scalzone]] and [[Toni Negri]], he was  one of the founders of the far-left organisation ''[[Potere Operaio]]'',<ref name="tramontopotop"/><ref name="cattivimaestri"/> and later he was a member of ''[[Autonomia Operaia]]''. He also led the wing of Potere Operaio called ''Lavoro Illegale'' ("Illegal Work").<ref name="fioroni">{{cite news|last=Scottoni|first=Franco|title=Fiori spiega i rapporti tra le BR e 'Autonomia'|url=http://ricerca.repubblica.it/repubblica/archivio/repubblica/1987/01/14/fioroni-spiega-rapporti-tra-le-br-autonomia.html|accessdate=17 January 2011|newspaper=La Repubblica|date=14 January 1987}}</ref>

With Negri, Scalzone, and others, he was charged with the publication of subversive magazines in 1979<ref name="cattivimaestri"/> but he escaped capture.<ref name="tramontopotop"/> In 1980 he was absolved, but one year later he was  condemned to ten years of imprisonment in another trial  for insurrectional activity and participation in the [[kidnapping and murder of Aldo Moro]].<ref name="cattivimaestri"/> In particular, he was accused of having acted as a negotiator (through one of the kidnappers, [[Valerio Morucci]]) between the [[Italian Socialist Party]] and the terrorists who were allegedly detaining Moro.<ref name="memoriesguerrilla">{{cite book|last=Hansen|first=Ann|title=Direct Action: memoirs of an urban guerrilla|year=2001|publisher=AK Press|location=Canada|pages=25|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=9HRClitXq7UC&q=%22franco+piperno%22&pg=PA25|isbn=9781896357409}}</ref> Documents left by the journalist [[Mino Pecorelli]] after his murder also hinted at an involvement of Piperno in the kidnapping.<ref name="puppetmasters">{{cite book|last=Willan|first=Philip|title=Puppetmasters: The Political Use of Terrorism in Italy|orig-year=1991|year=2002|publisher=Constable and Company|pages=185|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=9g-UIMo1SaYC&q=%22franco+piperno%22&pg=PA185|isbn=9781469710846}}</ref> Piperno then lived in exile for several years, first in France thanks to the [[Mitterrand doctrine]] and then in Canada, where he also obtained a position at the [[University of Montreal]]<ref name="cattivimaestri"/> and then at the Faculte St. Jean at the University of Alberta in Edmonton. Most of the charges were later dropped, and the sentence was reduced to four years.<ref name="cattivimaestri"/>

Piperno returned to Italy from Canada in 1990,<ref name="intervista_rimedio">{{cite book|last=Rimedio|first=Vincenzo|title=Il volto dell'essere|publisher=Rubbettino|pages=105|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=BsX-Tk2id8wC&q=%22franco+piperno%22+%22potere+operaio%22&pg=PA105|isbn=9788849814033|year=2005}}</ref> and became active locally in his hometown, [[Cosenza]], creating the cultural association ''Ciroma''. In January 1996 his car was hit by four handgun bullets.<ref name="bullets">{{cite news|last=Macri`|first=Carlo|title=Cosenza, quattro colpi di pistola contro l' auto di Franco Piperno|url=http://archiviostorico.corriere.it/1996/gennaio/28/Cosenza_quattro_colpi_pistola_contro_co_0_9601281456.shtml|accessdate=17 January 2011|newspaper=Corriere della Sera|date=28 January 1996}}</ref> In May 1996, Piperno became a  member of the local council of the city of Cosenza.<ref name="assessore">{{cite news|last=Fertilio|first=Dario|title=E Piperno diventa assessore|url=http://archiviostorico.corriere.it/1996/maggio/07/Piperno_diventa_assessore_co_0_9605078557.shtml|accessdate=17 January 2011|date=7 May 1996}}</ref>

Piperno died on 13 January 2025 in Cosenza, at the age of 82.<ref>{{cite news |title=È morto a 82 anni Franco Piperno, tra i fondatori del gruppo di sinistra extraparlamentare Potere operaio |url=https://www.ilpost.it/2025/01/14/morto-franco-piperno/ |access-date=14 January 2025 |publisher=Il Post |date=14 January 2025}}</ref>
